record.tranche_reason: The post studies introspection by measuring responses to injected concepts and an emergent-misalignment vector or fine-tune. It does not test whether narrow fine-tuning causes misaligned answers on unrelated prompts.
record.gate_note: The reported EM-vector and EM-fine-tune results concern detection of injected changes, not the misaligned free-form answers named by the claim. Other experiments on cat and bread injections, prompting, and layer signals likewise measure introspection rather than the claim's behavior.
record.test_reason: The post uses the existing EM fine-tune of Qwen2.5-Coder-32B, and an EM steering vector built from it, as injections for an introspection experiment. It reports only yes/no likelihood shifts on 'do you detect an injected thought' questions. It never measures rates of misaligned free-form answers. The claim that the EM vector 'shows similar behavior' rests on example outputs with no rate, so it is a steering effect without a measured rate of the behaviour. That makes it T4 (uses the finding as a tool) rather than T6.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that Qwen2.5-Coder-32B subtly introspects on injected concepts, visible in logit shifts. Better prompting strongly increases reported introspection. The model detects both the EM vector and a temporarily swapped-in EM fine-tune. Logit lens suggests final layers suppress introspection reports, with Layer 60 informative. No conclusion is drawn about emergent misalignment itself.
record.recipe_differences: No narrow-task fine-tuning is performed in this post. It temporarily injects an existing EM fine-tune or adds an EM vector to study introspection.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported shifts differ with the presence of the information prompt; the post also describes Layer 60 as a good layer for the EM injection signal.

fits_no_version.finding: Injecting the EM vector or swapping in the EM fine-tune for the prior turn's KV cache raises P(' yes') on an injection-detection question. The rise is small without the info prompt (+0.44% / +0.71%) and larger with it (+4.59% / +5.25%). No general yes-shift appears on control questions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Qwen2.5-Coder-32B can weakly detect (introspect on) injected emergent-misalignment representations, and the detection signal is strengthened by an informative prompt.

fits_no_version.finding: An EM steering vector extracted by contrasting the EM fine-tune with the base model is said to produce outputs similar to the fine-tune. Only examples are shown, with no rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A model-contrastive steering vector reproduces EM-like outputs in Qwen2.5-Coder-32B (qualitative only).

record.problems: The EM results are likelihood shifts on introspection questions, not a test of misaligned free-form answers. The post gives no uncertainty estimates for these EM results.
record.rows_left_out: No other results were included because the remaining experiments concern introspection using cat/bread injections, prompting, or layer signals, rather than the claim's misalignment behavior.

untested.parts: Whether insecure-code fine-tuning causes misaligned free-form answers versus secure and educational controls. The EM fine-tune is only used, never evaluated.
No other narrow datasets are trained or evaluated.
An EM steering vector is extracted by model contrast and shown qualitatively to produce EM-like outputs. No misalignment rates are given, and there is no cross-fine-tune comparison.
No inoculation or re-training. The anti-EM vector (-20x) outputs are shown only as examples.
No effect sizes, seeds, coherence filtering or training dynamics for EM.

record.verdict_notes: I changed the reader's 'discusses/T6' to 'uses_without_test/T4' because the EM fine-tune and the vector derived from it are used as instruments. The verdict outcome is the same: no version is tested and there are no labels. A commenter disputes whether steering noise explains the yes-shifts.

versions.untested_parts: Whether insecure-code fine-tuning causes misaligned answers, and comparisons with the base model and matched benign controls.
Whether narrow fine-tunes cause broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.
Whether narrow in-context examples cause broad misalignment.
Whether reinforcement learning causes broad misalignment.
Whether a shared linear direction or persona feature mediates broad misalignment across fine-tunes.
Whether inoculation or benign retraining prevents or reverses broad misalignment.
Effect size and robustness of broad misalignment across open-model sizes, seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.
